methodologyNotes:
Roster covers thirteen heat guns spanning budget DIY (Harbor Freight/Warrior 56434, Wagner HT1000), mainstream contractor-grade corded (Wagner FURNO 700, Genesis GHG1500A, Porter-Cable PC1500HG, SEEKONE SDL2816), professional/industrial (Makita HG6031VK, Steinel HG 2320 E, Bosch GHG 20-63, Master Appliance Proheat PH-1100A), and the emerging 2026 cordless class (DeWalt DCE530B, Milwaukee M18 2688-20, Ryobi P3150 18V ONE+). Specs verified 2026-08-01 primarily against manufacturer product pages (Wagner Spraytech, DeWalt, Milwaukee, Makita, Bosch Professional, Ryobi) with corroboration from retailers and distributors (Ohio Power Tool, Home Depot listings mirrored via WebStaurantStore, ITM.com, GlobalTestSupply, Pro Tool Reviews, Harbor Freight). max_temp_f and airflow_cfm are converted to imperial units from the manufacturer's native °C/L-per-min figures where no imperial figure is published (Bosch GHG 20-63, SEEKONE SDL2816); converted values are noted per-product. null means a spec is not published anywhere verified for that exact model, never a guess. temp_settings and airflow_cfm are recorded as descriptive strings (not bare numbers) because most heat guns expose either a fixed count of discrete settings or a continuously-variable dial with a documented range, and collapsing that distinction to one integer would misrepresent the control scheme.

Adversarial corrections to the seed list: (1) 'DeWalt DWHG501' does not exist in DeWalt's current or archived US catalog (confirmed by direct DeWalt.com search and cross-checked against every retailer catalog reachable this session) — it was replaced with the real DeWalt DCE530B 20V MAX cordless heat gun, the actual DeWalt SKU buyers cross-shop against the Milwaukee M18 2688-20 and Ryobi P3150 in the 2026 cordless-heat-gun segment. (2) 'SEEKONE 1800W' is sold under several near-identical Amazon SKUs; the base SDL2816 (2 airflow/temperature modes, no LCD, official iseekone.com model code, ~$40) was used because it is the variant retailers list under the plain '1800W' name — a separate SEEKONE SKU adds an LCD display and memory function at a higher price and is a distinct product. (3) The literal 'Master Appliance Proheat PH-1100' base dual-temperature SKU (500°F/1000°F) is listed as discontinued by multiple distributors (e.g. CenturyTool); the actively-sold, current PH-1100A 'Quick Touch' (3 temperatures including a 1200°F setting, adjustable 9-18 CFM) was used instead as the model buyers can actually still buy and compare in 2026. (4) 'Bosch GHG 20-63' is Bosch's international 'Professional' (blue) line model rated 230-240V/2000W; Bosch does not officially import or sell this exact SKU through Bosch North America, and boschtools.com (the US storefront) does not list it. The USD price found (Walmart Marketplace / BeyondTools) is a third-party importer/reseller listing, not a Bosch USA MSRP, and a US buyer would need a step-down transformer to run it — this is flagged in the product's priceNote rather than presented as a native US retail price. (5) Genesis GHG1500A and Porter-Cable PC1500HG have solid, multiply-corroborated specs, but genesispowertools.com and portercable.com blocked automated fetches (403 / timeout) every attempt this session; their specs are sourced from the manufacturer's own listing text as mirrored verbatim across independent retailer pages (Amazon, WebstaurantStore, McLendon's, Busy Beaver for Genesis; Pro Tool Reviews for Porter-Cable), and no freely-licensed direct product image could be resolved to a static file URL for either, so image is omitted for both rather than guessed.

products.name: Wagner FURNO 700 Heat Gun
products.priceNote: Current price on Wagner's own store (wagnerspraytech.com); model number 0503070

specs.temp_settings: 117 discrete settings via digital dial (125-1300°F range)

products.provenance: Wagner's own product pages confirm 1500W / 5100 BTU, 125-1300°F range with 117 settings, five fan speeds plus cool-down, LCD screen with push-button controls, two included nozzles (glass protector, flare), integrated hands-free stand, and a $85.00 price. Airflow CFM and weight are not published on either Wagner page and are left null rather than estimated. Image confirmed as a real, on-brand product photo (yellow/black Wagner FURNO 700 with LCD readout) fetched directly from Wagner's own CDN.

products.name: DeWalt DCE530B 20V MAX Cordless Heat Gun (Tool Only)
products.priceNote: Current retail (WebstaurantStore, item #230DCE530B); DeWalt.com does not display a price. Other retailers (Home Depot/Acme) list $166.99-$199.99 for the same bare tool depending on promotion.
products.provenance: CORRECTED FROM SEED: the seed model 'DWHG501' does not exist anywhere in DeWalt's US catalog (confirmed via direct site search); replaced with DCE530B, DeWalt's real current 20V MAX cordless heat gun. DeWalt's official product page confirms up to 990°F/532°C max output, two temperature settings, 6.7 CFM airflow, lock-on trigger, LED light, and included flat + hook nozzle attachments (no LCD). Battery/charger sold separately (bare tool). Tool weight is not published on the DeWalt page; left null. Price $178.99 confirmed on a retailer catalog page that lists this exact SKU alongside heat guns from other brands; broader retail pricing runs $166.99-$199.99. Image is DeWalt's own official product asset, confirmed as a real photo showing the DCE530B with its two chrome nozzle attachments.

products.name: Milwaukee M18 2688-20 Compact Heat Gun (Tool Only)
products.priceNote: Current MSRP per Ohio Power Tool; Milwaukee does not display consumer pricing on its own site
products.provenance: Milwaukee's official page confirms sub-7-second heat-up, 6.4in compact length, guarded nozzle, ladder hook, REDLINK PLUS temperature management, and M18 REDLITHIUM battery compatibility, but does not publish max temperature, airflow, wattage, weight, or nozzle-attachment count. Ohio Power Tool corroborates identity and adds max temperature 875°F, net tool weight 1.7 lb, and MSRP $159.00. Temperature-settings count, airflow CFM, and nozzle-attachment count remain undocumented across every source checked and are left null rather than guessed (the compact head appears to be a fixed, non-interchangeable nozzle design, but no source states an attachment count). Image is the official Milwaukee product photo hosted by Ohio Power Tool, confirmed showing the red/black M18 compact heat gun.

products.name: Makita HG6031VK Variable Temperature Heat Gun Kit
products.priceNote: No price published on makitatools.com and no independent US retailer page could be fetched this session to confirm a current figure
products.provenance: Makita's official product page confirms 122-1022°F range across a 9-position numbered dial (analog control, no LCD), two airflow settings (7 and 14 CFM), 1800W, 1.5 lb tool weight, 6.6ft cord, rubberized pistol grip, integrated rear stand, overheat protection, and an included carrying case (hence the 'K' kit suffix). Nozzle attachments are 'sold separately' per the page with no fixed included count, so left null. No price is published on the manufacturer page; this session's retailer fetch attempts for an independent price returned no usable content, so priceUsd is left null rather than estimated. Image is Makita's own official kit photo (heat gun plus case), confirmed as a real product photo.

products.name: Steinel HG 2320 E Professional Heat Gun
products.priceNote: Price varies significantly by kit configuration/retailer: $331.50 (GlobalTestSupply, plastic case kit), $290-367 range seen at Walmart/eBay depending on case type. No steinel.us/steinel.net US price could be fetched directly (both connection-reset or 403'd this session).

specs.temp_settings: 2 stages (continuously variable within stage 2) plus 4 programmable presets

products.provenance: Steinel's own US/international product pages (steinel.us, steineltools.net) returned connection errors or unparseable PDFs every attempt this session, so specs are sourced from GlobalTestSupply's distributor page and independently corroborated verbatim (120-1200°F, 4-13 CFM, 2.19 lb, 1600W) by ITM.com's listing. Both distributor pages and the Amazon listing (B0C34D1MN7) agree on: LCD display, residual-heat indicator, 4 included nozzles, and 4 customizable temperature/airflow programs. Image confirmed via direct fetch as a real photo of the Steinel HG 2320 E kit (heat gun, case, and 4 nozzle attachments).

products.name: Bosch GHG 20-63 Professional Heat Gun
products.priceNote: CORRECTION: Bosch does not officially sell this SKU in the US. This is Bosch's international 230-240V 'Professional' line model; boschtools.com (US site) does not list it. $164.99 is a third-party importer/reseller listing (Walmart Marketplace); BeyondTools separately lists it at $138.00. Not a Bosch USA MSRP, and US buyers need a step-down transformer to run it on 120V.

specs.temp_settings: continuously variable in 10°C (18°F) steps, 2 airflow stages

products.provenance: Bosch's own international Professional-line page (bosch-professional.com, order no. 0 601 2A6 2L0) confirms 50-630°C (converted: 122-1166°F) continuously variable in 10°C steps, 150-500 L/min airflow (converted: 5.3-17.7 CFM) across 2 stages, 2000W at 240V, 0.65kg (converted: 1.43 lb), a cold/cooling stage, and thermal overload protection; no LCD is mentioned or shown. boschtools.com (Bosch's official US storefront) does not carry this model under any US-market SKU found this session — every US 'price' for it traces to importer/reseller listings (Walmart Marketplace $164.99, BeyondTools $138.00), not a Bosch North America MSRP, which is flagged rather than presented as native. Nozzle-attachment count is not documented for the bare (non-kit) SKU used here, so left null. Image is Bosch's own official product photo (small 166x164 resolution as served by Bosch's CDN, but a real, correctly-identified photo of the blue GHG 20-63).

products.name: Ryobi P3150 18V ONE+ Heat Gun (Tool Only)
products.priceNote: Current price on ryobitools.com (bare tool; P193 6Ah battery sold separately)
products.provenance: Ryobi's product page and its support-site mirror independently confirm identical figures: 875°F max temperature, 6 CFM airflow, 1.4 lb tool weight, sub-10-second heat-up, one concentrator and one deflector nozzle included, LED work light, and $84.00 price. Neither page states a discrete temperature-settings count (the tool appears to run at a single fixed operating temperature rather than a selectable range) or mentions an LCD; both are recorded accordingly (settings null, lcd_display false based on the absence of any display in official photography and copy). Image is Ryobi's own official product photo, confirmed showing the green/black P3150 cordless heat gun.

products.name: Porter-Cable PC1500HG 1500-Watt Heat Gun
products.priceNote: ~$34 MSRP per Pro Tool Reviews; portercable.com does not display a price and retailer prices commonly run $30-45

specs.temp_settings: variable temperature control dial (continuous, per manufacturer); one Amazon listing title separately describes it as 'dual temperature settings' — not corroborated by the manufacturer page

products.provenance: portercable.com's own product listing (retrieved via search index after direct fetch timed out; content quoted verbatim matches the manufacturer's copy) states: 1500W motor, 19 CFM air output, 120-1150°F range via a variable temperature control dial, dual fan-speed selector (high/low), integrated hands-free stand, hanging hook, 6ft cord, and 2 lb weight. Pro Tool Reviews (independently fetched) corroborates the 2 lb weight and states an MSRP of 'around $34.' A conflicting Amazon listing title calls this 'Dual Temperature Settings' rather than a continuous dial; this discrepancy is noted rather than silently resolved. No freely-licensed direct product image could be resolved to a static file URL this session (Home Depot, Walmart, and ToolNut/ToolUp all blocked or CAPTCHA'd automated fetches); image key omitted rather than guessed.

products.name: Genesis GHG1500A Dual-Temperature Heat Gun
products.priceNote: No current USD price could be confirmed via direct manufacturer or retailer fetch this session; historically sold in the $25-35 range at mass retailers

specs.temp_settings: 2 (572°F low / 1000°F high) plus off, via 3-position rocker switch

products.provenance: genesispowertools.com (the manufacturer's own page for this product) returned HTTP 403 to every automated fetch attempt this session, so it is cited as corroboration of identity/URL only, not as the content source. Specs are the manufacturer's own listing text, mirrored verbatim and in full agreement across independently-indexed retailer pages (Amazon, WebstaurantStore, McLendon's, Busy Beaver): 120V/60Hz, 12.5A, dual output 750W/1500W corresponding to 572°F/1000°F, 10/17 CFM air volume, 1.2 lb net weight, integrated stand, 2 included deflector nozzles plus 1 reflector nozzle plus 1 air-reduction nozzle (4 total), and a 2-year warranty. No freely-licensed direct product image could be resolved to a static file URL this session (Amazon serves images via JS this pipeline can't resolve to a stable file link, and Home Depot/Grainger/other distributor pages all blocked automated fetches); image key omitted rather than guessed. No current USD price could be independently confirmed via a fetched page, so priceUsd is left null.

products.name: SEEKONE SDL2816 1800W Heat Gun
products.priceNote: Current price at PremiumVials.com for the base (non-LCD) SDL2816 variant
products.provenance: CLARIFIED FROM SEED: 'SEEKONE 1800W' covers several near-identical Amazon SKUs; used here is the base SDL2816 model (per iseekone.com's own model code), matching the seed's plain '1800W' naming and the widely-sold Amazon ASIN B07DX4PL1M. Confirmed: 1800W, 122-1202°F (50-650°C) across 2 modes (Mode I 50-350°C/300 L/min, Mode II 50-650°C/500 L/min — converted to 10.6-17.7 CFM), ceramic heating element, overheat protection, 4 nozzles, 0.9kg (1.98 lb), $40.39 at PremiumVials. A separate SEEKONE SKU adds an LCD digital display with memory function at a higher price point and is a distinct product, not this one. Image confirmed via direct fetch as a real photo of the yellow/black SEEKONE unit with its analog dial and 4 nozzle attachments laid out.

products.name: Wagner HT1000 Heat Gun
products.priceNote: Current price on Wagner's own store (store.wagnerspraytech.com); model number 0503008
products.provenance: Wagner's own store page and the corroborating Amazon listing agree: 1200W / 4100 BTU, dual heat settings of 750°F and 1000°F via a two-speed switch, corrosion-resistant nozzle, integrated hanging hook, 1.5 lb weight, and $29.99 price. Airflow CFM is not published by Wagner and is left null. Fetched product image shows the HT1000 kit with 3 included metal nozzle attachments (straight, angled flare, and slotted reflector), so nozzle_attachments is recorded as 3 based on the confirmed photo rather than left null.

products.name: Master Appliance Proheat PH-1100A Quick Touch Heat Gun Kit
products.priceNote: No price listed on masterappliance.com; Walmart's listing page was CAPTCHA-blocked to automated fetch this session
products.provenance: CORRECTED FROM SEED: the literal base 'PH-1100' (dual-temp 500°F/1000°F, 1300W, 16 CFM) is listed as discontinued at multiple distributors (e.g. CenturyTool: 'no longer in stock'). Replaced with the current, actively-sold PH-1100A 'Quick Touch' 3-temperature model, confirmed on Master Appliance's own official product page: 3 selectable temperatures (ambient, 600°F/315°C, 1200°F/649°C), 2 adjustable airflow levels (9 and 18 CFM), 1.9 lb unit weight (10 lb as a cased kit), and a kit including spreader and shrink-tubing nozzle attachments (2 total). Wattage is not stated on the manufacturer page for this specific model and is left null rather than inferred from the sibling PH-1100. No price could be confirmed via a directly fetched page this session. Image is Master Appliance's own official product photo, confirmed showing the red/black PH-1100A with its rotary temperature dial.

products.name: Warrior 56434 1500W Dual-Temperature Heat Gun (Harbor Freight)
products.priceNote: Current price on harborfreight.com; sold exclusively through Harbor Freight Tools
products.provenance: CLARIFIED FROM SEED CATEGORY: Harbor Freight's budget heat gun house brand was 'Chicago Electric' (e.g. model 96289) and has since been largely superseded by the 'Warrior' house brand; model 56434 is the current directly-equivalent 1500W dual-temperature unit and is the one actually for sale on harborfreight.com today, so it was used as the representative current budget/big-box entry rather than a discontinued Chicago Electric SKU. Harbor Freight's own product page confirms 1500W, 11.25A, max 1000°F across high/low settings, and 1.5 lb weight. Airflow CFM and nozzle-attachment count are not published on the product page or in the linked manual (which this session could only retrieve as an unparseable binary PDF), so both are left null. Image is Harbor Freight's own cached product photo; confirmed as a real (small/low-resolution but genuine) photo of the tool, distinct from Harbor Freight's generic 'no image available' placeholder graphic which was independently checked and ruled out.
